subject: Zenith PoC — model slate + ops summary & next actions
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Zara Khan <zara.khan@zenith.ai>, Tom Evans <tom.evans@zenith.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Zenith PoC — model slate + ops summary & next actions

Hi Zara / Tom — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and recommended model slate for the PoC plus operational asks so we can move to a timed pilot. TL;DR: narrowed to three candidate models with clear tradeoffs below; attached prompt set + benchmark PDF + cost/latency estimate.

Recommended candidate slate (prioritized):
- Redwood-4x (default): best quality on our prompt sets, easy signal for safety regressions, estimated median latency ~90ms on our hosted node; cost higher (~2.8x baseline).
- RW-3-Quant (4-bit): competitive quality for retrieval-heavy flows, 25–35% lower token cost, median latency ~110ms, 99p latency risk under sustained bursts.
- OpenLlama-Large (quantized): lowest cost, acceptable for low-complexity completions, weaker instruction-following on narrow tasks; median latency ~130ms.

Key tradeoffs and risks:
- Quality regressions: Redwood-4x has the smallest regression surface; RW-3-Quant requires prompt calibration to avoid hallucination on long retrieval contexts. We'll include regression guards (prompt slices and eval thresholds).
- Latency SLOs: if 99th percentile is critical (>250ms unacceptable), we recommend Redwood-4x with prefix-caching enabled and continuous batching disabled for interactive routes.
- Cost: see attached cost_latency_estimates.csv for monthly estimates at 1M tokens/day.

Deliverables attached: zenith_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt slices + evaluation labels), zenith_benchmarks_20270627.pdf (benchmarks for the three models), cost_latency_estimates.csv. Also linking the benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/zenith/benchmarks_20270627

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the two target flows you want covered in the PoC (search-assist and case-summarization).
2) We run a 2-week sandbox evaluation with your 5k sample records + our prompt set (we'll provision an eval sandbox).
3) Joint review at day 10 for quality checks and rollback criteria before move to a week-long live pilot.

Can we lock a 30–45m sync on Tue/Wed next week? I proposed times on the calendar invite.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: zenith_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, zenith_benchmarks_20270627.pdf, cost_latency_estimates.csv

Subject: Re: Zenith PoC — model slate + ops summary & next actions

Thanks Priya — useful summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we confirm flows: 
1) For the '99th percentile latency' you mentioned risk on RW-3-Quant under bursts — can you confirm expected p99 numbers at our target concurrency (we're planning 40 rps peak)?
2) On quality regressions: do you have a short checklist of the prompt-slices we should watch and a recommended guardrail policy (thresholds and fallback model)?
3) Budget: procurement wants a ballpark for monthly spend for the two flows at 1M tokens/day so we can greenlight the SOW.

If you can send the p99 table + the prompt-slice checklist, I can share them with Tom and Procurement. Also please cc procure@zenith.ai on the SOW thread once available.

— Zara
Head of Product, Zenith AI

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Zara Khan <zara.khan@zenith.ai>, Tom Evans <tom.evans@zenith.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zenith PoC — model slate + ops summary & next actions

Hi Zara — answers inline and attached the requested artifacts.

On Sun, Jun 27, 2027 at 1:02 PM Zara Khan <zara.khan@zenith.ai> wrote:
> 1) For the '99th percentile latency' ... can you confirm expected p99 numbers at our target concurrency (we're planning 40 rps peak)?

- Attached 'cost_latency_estimates.csv' includes a p50/p95/p99 breakdown at 40 RPS for each candidate. Snapshot: Redwood-4x p99 ~210ms (with prefix caching + 1x batching), RW-3-Quant p99 ~340ms (risk increases on sustained bursts), OpenLlama-Large p99 ~420ms. If strict p99 < 300ms is required, we recommend Redwood-4x or a dedicated capacity pool for RW-3-Quant.

> 2) On quality regressions: do you have a short checklist of the prompt-slices we should watch and a recommended guardrail policy (thresholds and fallback model)?

- Prompt slices in zenith_prompt_set_v1.jsonl marked with keys: 'legal_terms', 'multi-doc-summary', 'abbrev-heavy'. We recommend monitoring ROUGE / exact-match for 'multi-doc-summary' and hallucination rate (false entities) for 'legal_terms'.
- Guardrail policy (recommended):
  * Eval thresholds: fail if multi-doc-summary ROUGE-L drops >6 points vs baseline or hallucination rate >3%.
  * Fallback: route failing requests to Redwood-4x (if cost acceptable) or return a conservative 'insufficient confidence' response to the client.

> 3) Budget: procurement wants a ballpark for monthly spend...

- See line items in cost_latency_estimates.csv. For the two flows at ~1M tokens/day: Redwood-4x ≈ $28k/mo, RW-3-Quant ≈ $11k/mo, OpenLlama-Large ≈ $6k/mo (these include token + infra amortized). We'll confirm with Finance for exact commit tiers.

Attachments: cost_latency_estimates.csv, zenith_benchmarks_20270627.pdf, zenith_prompt_set_v1.jsonl
Links: https://drive.google.com/zenith/benchmarks_20270627, HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/zen-347

Proposed meeting times (same invite I sent): Tue 10:00 or Wed 14:30 PT — please pick one and I'll book. Also cc'd Ben/Monica/Karthik to help scope SOW and dedicated capacity options.

Best — Priya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Internal note — copying into the thread so procurement sees context when we share the SOW. Quick commercial and execution checklist before the Tue/Wed sync: 
- Deal: ZEN-347 (HubSpot above). Prospect is price sensitive but values p99 latency and regression monitoring.
- Ask: prepare two SOW variants — hosted PoC (no commit) and 3-month dedicated pool (committed discount). Include an option for a one-time calibration service (prompt tuning + eval harness) priced as a professional services line.
- Discount guardrails: we can offer up to 20% on hosted usage for the first 3 months; anything >20% requires RevOps approval.
- Ops: Monica — please prepare the sandbox provisioning checklist and the eval job (we should run the baseline bench within 48 hours of their sample data). Karthik — confirm quantization runbook and fallback routing config for RW-3-Quant.

I'll draft the SOW and attach SOW_draft_zenith.docx to the deal after Priya confirms the scope. Priya — can you confirm which two flows to include (search-assist + case-summary as proposed)? If yes I'll finalize the SOW draft and loop Procurement.

Thanks — Ben
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
